subtopics.title: Compressions, Rarefactions and the Longitudinal Wave

questions.question: In a longitudinal wave the particles of the medium vibrate:
options: Parallel to — in the same line as — the direction the wave travels
Perpendicular to the direction the wave travels
In circles about their rest positions

questions.question: A region of a longitudinal wave where the particles are crowded together, with higher pressure and density, is called a:
The wavelength of a longitudinal wave is measured:
options: From a compression to the next rarefaction
From the rest line to a compression
Between two successive compressions (or two successive rarefactions)
Across the width of the slinky

questions.question: Which statement about the wave equations is correct for longitudinal waves?
options: Neither applies — new formulae are needed
Both f = 1/T and v = fλ apply unchanged — only the picture differs, not the mathematics

subtopics.title: Sound as a Longitudinal Wave, and the Speed of the Medium

questions.question: An electric bell ringing inside a jar falls silent as the air is pumped out because:
options: Sound needs a medium — with no particles there are no compressions to travel
The hammer stops striking in a vacuum
The glass absorbs all the sound
Sound travels too fast to hear in a vacuum

questions.question: The correct order of the speed of sound, fastest first, is:
options: Solids, liquids, gases — the closer and more strongly bound the particles, the faster the disturbance is passed on
The speed is the same in all three

questions.question: Shouting more loudly makes the sound:
options: Travel at exactly the same speed — speed is a property of the medium, not the source

questions.question: The audible range of human hearing is approximately:
The pitch of a note is determined by its:
options: FREQUENCY — high frequency gives high pitch

questions.question: Plucking the same guitar string harder changes the:
options: LOUDNESS only — a bigger amplitude delivers more energy, while the frequency and so the pitch stay the same
Speed of the sound in air

questions.question: A guitar and a marimba playing the identical note sound different because of their:
options: QUALITY — the waveform, set by the mix of fainter higher frequencies added to the main one

questions.question: A hooter sounds at 850 Hz. With the speed of sound in air taken as 340 m·s⁻¹, the wavelength is:

subtopics.title: Echoes, Ultrasound, and the Factor of Two

questions.question: The correct relationship for an echo off a surface a distance d away is:
options: d = (v × Δt) ÷ 2 — because the sound travels to the surface AND back

questions.question: A hiker hears an echo 1,2 s after shouting, with sound at 340 m·s⁻¹. The cliff is:
A sonar pulse returns after 0,4 s through seawater at 1 500 m·s⁻¹. The depth is:
Ultrasound is preferred to X-rays for scanning a developing foetus because it:
options: Is NOT ionising radiation, so it does not damage cells

subtopics.title: The Slinky and the Taxi Queue

questions.question: In the taxi-queue model, the 'squash' that runs up the line represents a:
What makes the queue a longitudinal model rather than a transverse one?
options: The people are standing in a straight line
The people shuffle forward and back ALONG the same line the squash travels

questions.question: The thin, stretched-out patch just behind each squash represents a:

subtopics.title: Why Sound Is a Queue of Air

questions.question: Your eardrum registers a sound when:
options: A squash of crowded air arrives and pushes it in
Air travels all the way from the speaker into your ear
Light from the source reaches it
The air in your ear heats up

questions.question: The queue analogy explains the speed order because:
options: People standing shoulder to shoulder pass the squash along almost instantly, while people standing far apart take much longer
The front of the queue moves first

questions.question: Approximate speeds of sound in steel, water and air are:
You see lightning before you hear thunder because:
options: Thunder is quieter than lightning is bright
Light reaches you almost immediately while the sound trudges through air at about 340 m·s⁻¹

subtopics.title: High, Loud, and the Round Trip

questions.question: Pitch is 'how fast' and loudness is 'how hard'. In wave language that means:
options: Pitch is set by frequency; loudness is set by amplitude
Pitch is set by amplitude; loudness is set by frequency
Both are set by the wave speed
Both are set by the waveform

questions.question: Recognising a familiar voice in a crowded room depends on the sound's:
options: QUALITY — the particular shape of its wave, made by the faint extra tones mixed with the main one

questions.question: An echo returns after 1,2 s. Sound at 340 m·s⁻¹ covers 408 m in that time. The reflecting cliff is:
options: 408 m away — the sound travelled 408 m
204 m away — 408 m is the whole round trip, so halve it

questions.question: Ultrasound is:
options: Sound of frequency above about 20 000 Hz — too high for human ears, used by bats and by hospital scanners
